subject: Convoy launch: runway forecast, short-term quota uplift & routing asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Desai <samir@convoy.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Convoy launch: runway forecast, short-term quota uplift & routing asks

Team —

Quick heads-up from the Convoy pilot planning call this morning. They pushed the public beta window to the first week of April and want a phased ramp: 50k API calls/day Day 1 -> 250k/day by Day 7. Attached is the forecast workbook (convoy_traffic_forecast_v3.xlsx) they shared. Key asks for us:

- Short-term quota uplift: they need ~3x token quota for the first 72 hours (spike window) to avoid 429s.
- Temporary routing: prefer us to route low-latency traffic to the us-west cluster and overflow to a cheaper quantized variant if latency-backed nodes are saturated.
- Canary plan: staged rollout with a 5% canary, 25% after 12h, full after 48h.

Notes: they care about tail latency more than cost during launch. Procurement will require a written SLA exemption and an uplift credit for the first 30 days.

Action items: can product confirm if we can set a temporary quota bump scoped to their API key for the first 72 hours and enable model-variant fallback routing? Also need infra to confirm surge capacity on us-west and any lead time for burst nodes.

Marissa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: convoy_traffic_forecast_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 tabs)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Convoy launch: runway forecast, short-term quota uplift & routing asks

+1 to quick answers + routing constraints.

Marissa — high level responses:
- Quota bump: we can do a scoped quota override on their API key for a defined window. Operations needs exact numbers (RPS / token budget) and a start/end time so we can schedule and monitor.
- Model fallback: product supports routing policies, but we need to validate compatibility matrix between the primary model and the cheaper quantized variant (same tokenizer, output parity). If not compatible, fallback will require response normalization.
- Canary tooling: Redwood Console supports incremental rollout percentages; no infra changes required for 5% -> 25% -> 100% pattern.

Ask from Product: Laura — can you validate model variant compatibility and give guidance on expected quality delta (rough estimate OK) between primary and quantized fallback for chat/generation?
Ask from Infra: Jonas — can you confirm burst node availability in us-west and approximate warm-up time if we need to spin additional capacity at T+0?

I can draft the SLA exemption template once we have numbers.

Karthik
Senior PM, Product@Redwood
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Convoy launch: runway forecast, short-term quota uplift & routing asks

Quick infra readout:
- Current us-west pool has ~120 vGPU slots that are unconstrained today. Typical baseline occupancy is 65%. We can reserve an additional 40 slots for a 72h uplift with ~6 hours lead time to allocate and validate networking.
- Warm-up: if we need new instances we can provision in ~90 minutes but kernel optimizations and KV cache priming take an extra ~2 hours to reach steady-state tail latency. Recommend reserving slots rather than live-provisioning at T+0.
- Monitoring: I will add a dedicated dashboard and set automated alerts for 95/99/99.9 latencies and queue depth.

Numbers we need from Marissa / Convoy: expected peak RPS, average tokens per request, absolute token budget for the 72h window. With those we can translate to vGPU-hours and confirm the 40-slot ask.

-Jonas
Head of Infra
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Convoy launch: runway forecast, short-term quota uplift & routing asks

Marissa / Karthik —
I spun up quick A/Bs against the quantized variant (redwood-qlt-v2) and primary (redwood-base-chat-3). Early results: for short prompts (<80 tokens) output quality delta is low for completion tasks; for multi-turn chat with long context (>1024 tokens) the quantized variant shows ~6-8% drop in intent recall on our internal metric. Latency difference: quantized variant reduces avg P95 by ~40ms.

Conclusion: fallback to redwood-qlt-v2 is reasonable for high-throughput, low-context requests (webhooks, single-step completions). For multi-turn flows (customer-facing conversational UI) we should keep primary or do partial routing based on request type.

I can produce a simple routing rule set:
- If tokens_est <= 120 AND request_type in [completion, rerank] -> fallback to redwood-qlt-v2
- Else -> primary model

If Marketing insists on cost-first fallback, we can route all low-latency endpoints to quantized for first 48 hours and then relax.

Laura
Product, Model Serving
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir@convoy.ai>, Olivia Park <ops@convoy.ai>, procurement@convoy.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Convoy launch: runway forecast, short-term quota uplift & routing asks

Samir / Olivia —
Thanks for the call earlier. Summarizing next steps and what Redwood will provide for the April beta: 

1) Temporary quota uplift: Redwood will provision a scoped quota override for Convoy's API key for a 72-hour launch window. Please confirm start time (proposed: 2027-04-05T08:00:00-07:00). We need the expected peak RPS and average tokens/request before we lock numbers.
2) Routing plan: we will enable the model-variant fallback rule set (Laura's proposal). We'll route low-token completion endpoints to redwood-qlt-v2 and keep multi-turn channels on primary.
3) Infra reservation: Jonas will reserve 40 vGPU slots in us-west and add a monitoring dashboard.
4) SLA & credits: we'll issue a 30-day cost uplift credit and a written SLA exemption for tail-latency objectives — procurement please advise on required language.

Attachments: SLO exemption draft (slo_exemption_request.pdf), traffic workbook (convoy_traffic_forecast_v3.xlsx).

Samir — please reply with the start timestamp and the following numbers ASAP: peak RPS (expected), avg tokens per request, percent of requests that are multi-turn (est). Once we have those we will finalize the quota numbers and schedule the reservation.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth roll.

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
